title: Machine-learning microscopy isolates micronucleated cells and reveals chromosome-abnormality formation
summary: The MAGIC platform used an XGBoost image classifier to identify and photolabel micronucleated cells for single-cell genome sequencing. In near-diploid human cell models, the selected cells exposed new chromosome-abnormality formation patterns, including dicentric-associated breakage-fusion-bridge events; measured baseline abnormalities approximately doubled in TP53-deficient cells, and chromosome losses outnumbered gains.
ai_technology: MAGIC adaptive imaging platform with an XGBoost micronuclei classifier
organization: European Molecular Biology Laboratory and German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), with collaborators

evidence.tested: In near-diploid human cell models, the selected cells exposed new chromosome-abnormality formation patterns, including dicentric-associated breakage-fusion-bridge events; measured baseline abnormalities approximately doubled in TP53-deficient cells, and chromosome losses outnumbered gains.
evidence.unknown: Findings come from near-diploid non-transformed cell lines and sequencing limited mainly to chromosome abnormalities larger than 200 kb in dividing cells. Micronucleated RPE-1 cells did not show significant CA enrichment, unlike MCF10A; spontaneous cell-line results do not establish cancer outcomes in patients.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning examined live confocal images, identified micronucleated cells and drove targeted photolabelling so selected cells could be sorted for downstream single-cell sequencing. The model enabled targeted sampling; it did not itself infer chromosome-abnormality mechanisms from sequence data.
